text:
maria: Ran nsys capture on dev-replica (ptx18). Quick summary: softmax_kernel_v2 is ~48% GPU time, kv_prefetcher thread spikes right before request boundaries, and we see repeated cudaMemcpyAsync stalls between launches. Perfetto shows gaps labeled 'idle' during the cache-miss path.

steve: Can you share the trace link? Agree NVTX ranges per request + per-kernel will make this much easier to correlate host prefetch and device kernels. Suggest names like `req:<rid>`, `req:<rid>:kv_prefetch`, `req:<rid>:kernel:softmax_v2`.

maria: Trace (filtered by req=0x2f9a): https://perf.server/trace/abc123 — open to everyone. My thinking: keep tags short but expressive, e.g. `r=1234|k=sm_v2|s=1` so we can grep in perfetto and export slices.

anya: Small perf note: avoid long strings in NVTX payloads. Use nvtxRangePushEx with colorId and a compact ascii tag (<=16 chars). Example prototype: 
```
char tag[16];
snprintf(tag,sizeof(tag),"r=%04x:k=%s", short_req, "sm2");
nvtxRangePushA(tag);
```
That keeps overhead tiny.

steve: Also add an explicit 'kernel_hint' range when we pick a kernel variant (fp16 vs int8 vs fallback). That way perfetto shows cost of fallback decisions: `req:123:kernel_hint:fp16`.

infra-bot: nsys capture job #452 finished for dev-replica-02 — /traces/452 (artifact available).

sam: Quick ops ask — when we add per-request ranges, please DO NOT put full UUIDs in NVTX names. Instead store a short mapping file (csv) from short_id -> full_request_uuid for later cross-ref. We'll avoid huge trace overhead and sensitive identifiers.

maria: Agreed. Plan for a PR: 1) add compact NVTX tags for "req", "batch", "kv_hit"/"kv_miss"/"kv_prefetch" and per-kernel ranges; 2) emit a host-side CSV mapping short_id -> full UUID (rotated per-capture); 3) run nsys/perfetto captures for batch sizes [1,4,8] and compare softmax kernel time + memcpy gaps.

anya: One more UX tip: use color coding for kv states: green = hit, red = miss, yellow = prefetch. Makes the perfetto timeline readable at a glance.

maria: Will implement. Also adding a top-level `batch:<bsize>` range that wraps the per-request kernels so we can measure batching heuristics effect. Will post nsys diffs once runs finish.

steve: :thumbsup:
